docker.//: OCI distribution (Docker registry v2). Digest-addressed blobs and manifests are content-addressed, hence immutable and cached forever; tags, tag lists and referrers are mutable, so they revalidate on a short window. _catalog is a dynamic listing. The catch-all is a short window rather than a redirect, so an unrecognised endpoint is never bounced to an origin the client has no credentials for. Layers are far larger than the artifacts this cache was sized for: check MinimumFreeDiskSpaceMb and the bucket lifecycle before enabling widely. RequestTimeoutSec needs no raising - it bounds the response head only, never the body - and IdleReadTimeoutSec, which does cover the body, bounds silence rather than duration, so a multi-gigabyte layer passes on any timing.

nuget.//: NuGet v3. Content under {id}/{version}/ is immutable - a published version cannot be replaced - so .nupkg/.snupkg/.nuspec are cached forever (no matching rule means no expiry). The rest are documents that grow and have to revalidate: the flat-container {id}/index.json version list, registration indexes and pages, the vulnerability index. No Redirect rule, unlike npm, because nothing here may carry a query string: an upstream URI is built from the routed path alone, so a query never leaves us and every distinct search would be answered from one cache entry. Search and autocomplete are therefore advertised away from these prefixes altogether - at nuget.org's own search hosts for the public feed, at the origin for the private Space ones, both from cache-redirector's Config.kt. A Redirect rule would carry the query - it appends the request's own to the Location - but it would also bounce the client to an origin it may hold no credential for, which is the same reason the docker catch-all above is a short window rather than a redirect.

cargo.//: Cargo. A published .crate is immutable - crates.io forbids replacing a version - so the download endpoints are cached forever. The two shapes are crates.io's own /crates/{crate}/{version}/download and a Space registry's /files/{crate}/{version}: a client reaches either one only because the index's config.json named it, and neither carries an extension to key on. static.rust-lang.org shares this profile because it is the same split - dated and version-pinned artifacts are immutable, while the channel-rust-{stable,beta,nightly} and rustup/release-stable.toml pointers are rewritten on every release and fall through to the catch-all. That catch-all is what makes the sparse index cacheable at all, against the intuition that a mutated document cannot be: the index is append-only apart from yanked, upstream serves it max-age=600 with a strong ETag, and revalidating on that window is what lets a resolve survive an upstream outage on the stale copy. Every eternal rule is anchored at the path end, or on a segment no mutable document here has, because an index cached forever is not recoverable short of a cache wipe.
